structuredIncident.summary: At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024 (Turn 2), the RHOB process area experienced a loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team prepared for maintenance. The air supply was restored by about 10:07 AM with no injuries reported.
structuredIncident.focalEvent: Loss of instrument-air pressure at the RHOB receiving station (P-R) between approximately 10:00 and 10:03, triggering an alarm while a maintenance preparation activity for the #1 slab caster dryer group was in progress.
structuredIncident.normalState: Instrument air supply to the RHOB process area is maintained within normal pressure bands; local controls show no complaints. The Utilities team has completed boundary preparation but not yet received formal release from Maintenance (M-A).
structuredIncident.eventState: Local indication at P-R dropped below alarm threshold, triggering AL-44 'COMP FAULT' display. Work was paused by the Utilities crew. Pressure recovered to normal levels before maintenance acceptance.

entities.name: #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system
entities.description: Equipment group D-101 undergoing planned maintenance; served by site air-header via north gallery and distributed through local routes to RHOB process area.

entities.name: Utilities team (U-A, U-B)

entities.name: Maintenance receiver (M-A)
entities.description: Personnel qualified in dryer-maintenance who had not yet accepted the work boundary as of initial notification.

# Utilities area and service directory

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

# Utilities area and service directory

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

# Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

Record ID: IA-I01

At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored. No injury is reported.

The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment. Supporting records will be provided as the investigation develops.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

citations.excerpt:
# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

citations.excerpt:
# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

citations.excerpt:
# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Utilities area and service directory

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.

# Utilities point register extract

Record ID: IA-P02 | Configuration revision: PR-12 | Effective: 2024-05-01

| Point | Location/input | Description and scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P-U | Site header H-U, north gallery | Pressure upstream of the 1SC distribution routes |
| P-R | RHOB receiving header H-R | Pressure at the RHOB instrument-air receiving station |
| C-11 RUN | C-11 starter auxiliary contact | Common-header compressor motor running indication; not a local flow proof |
| AL-44 | RHOB PLC low-pressure input from P-R | Active below 4.5 bar; clears above 5.0 bar |

AL-44 display text was retained as “COMP FAULT” from an earlier operator-screen template. PR-12 maps it to the receiving-header pressure condition, not to C-11's trip contact.

This register maps signals. It does not establish the state of any distribution valve or prove that every supply disturbance would appear in the selected sample export.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

# Utilities area and service directory

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.

citations.excerpt:
# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Utilities area and service directory

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.

This misattribution means one premise about which source contains the information is contradicted. Component 2 (alarm does not necessarily indicate trip) is supported by ⟦evidence:span:1ccc6519-6aaf-4b86-a53d-d6d1d3abb7c7:39fc6db3a8d03c1f:0-1054⟧ showing C-11 RUN = 1 throughout alarm window (lines 11-20) while pressure dropped and alarm occurred. # Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

parts.claimText: The alarm label 'COMP FAULT' displayed on the operator screen at AL-44 does not necessarily indicate a compressor trip, as S10 notes this text was retained from an earlier template and may map to receiving-header pressure conditions rather than C-11's actual motor status.
parts.establishes: S1 establishes that AL-44 display text 'COMP FAULT' was retained from an earlier operator-screen template (line 12) and maps to receiving-header pressure condition, not C-11 trip contact (line 13). S3 shows C-11 RUN = 1 during alarm occurrence (lines 11-20), confirming the compressor remained running while pressure dropped. This supports that COMP FAULT at AL-44 can indicate header pressure issues without indicating a motor trip.
parts.reason: The claim has two scope components: (1) record observation about alarm label origin and mapping, (2) actual-state about whether alarm necessarily indicates compressor trip. Component 1 is partially-established: S1 supports that AL-44 text maps to header pressure not motor status; however the claim incorrectly attributes this template note to S10 when evidence in S1 contains it. S10 actually covers personnel authorization without template discussion (lines 5-13). This misattribution means one premise about which source contains the information is contradicted. Component 2 (alarm does not necessarily indicate trip) is supported by S3 showing C-11 RUN = 1 throughout alarm window (lines 11-20) while pressure dropped and alarm occurred. Since the citation attribution to S10 lacks evidential support, the claim's assertion about source content is not established for that portion, creating a partially-established status overall.
missingPremises: The claim attributes the template retention note to S10, but this content appears in S1 not S10. S10 discusses personnel assignments (lines 5-13) with no mention of alarm templates or label retention.

Whether COMP FAULT can indicate both pressure conditions and motor trip status in different configurations is not fully documented; evidence shows only the present instance where pressure drop triggered the alarm while C-11 remained running.
What operational procedures determine when AL-44 maps to C-11 motor status versus receiving-header pressure is not specified in supplied records.
Whether any other record or configuration drawing specifies when COMP FAULT indicates trip versus header pressure conditions is unknown from this working set.

# Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

Record ID: IA-I01

At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored. No injury is reported.

The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment. Supporting records will be provided as the investigation develops.

# Utilities area and service directory

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

Record ID: IA-I01

At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored. No injury is reported.

The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment. Supporting records will be provided as the investigation develops.

citations.excerpt:
# Utilities area and service directory

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

citations.excerpt:
# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.

# Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

Record ID: IA-I01

At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored. No injury is reported.

The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment. Supporting records will be provided as the investigation develops.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

# Record and measurement conventions

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. # Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

Record ID: IA-I01

At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored. No injury is reported.

The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment. Supporting records will be provided as the investigation develops.

# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.

nodes.label: Loss of instrument-air pressure at the RHOB receiving station (P-R) between approximately 10:00 and 10:03, triggering an alarm while a maintenance preparation activity for the #1 slab caster dryer group was in progress.
nodes.detail: At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024 (Turn 2), the RHOB process area experienced a loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team prepared for maintenance. The air supply was restored by about 10:07 AM with no injuries reported.

nodes.label: The work was paused when instrument-air pressure loss occurred.
At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure.
A two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance.
The air supply was subsequently restored after work pause.
Point P-R monitors pressure at the RHOB instrument-air receiving station.
Crew at gallery. Boundary preparation in progress; maintenance release pending.
Alarm AL-44 (COMP FAULT) occurred at 10:00:32, was acknowledged at 10:03:14 and cleared at 10:06:24.

edges.rationale: The maintenance preparation activity (⟦finding:c43d1e32-0eaf-42f5-bead-89202632a02d⟧) was ongoing immediately before the instrument-air pressure loss event occurred, establishing temporal precedence and situational context.
edges.counterfactual: If no work had been in progress at that location or time, the incident might not have triggered a pause or alarm response related to operational safety during active tasks.
edges.competingExplanation: The pressure loss could have originated independently of any maintenance activity; however, ⟦finding:c43d1e32-0eaf-42f5-bead-89202632a02d⟧ provides context for why it was significant enough to warrant investigation and potential procedural review.
edges.evidenceGap: No evidence directly links the preparation activity itself as a cause or contributor to the pressure loss mechanism.

edges.rationale: The pending release of the boundary (condition) enabled the incident by allowing work to proceed without a formally verified isolation state.
edges.counterfactual: If the maintenance boundary had been fully released and accepted prior to 10:00, the condition would have changed from 'preparation only' to 'accepted', potentially preventing reliance on an unverified configuration or triggering additional checks before proceeding with work that affected air supply.
edges.competingExplanation: The incident could be attributed solely to a mechanical failure of the compressor (C-11) independent of boundary status, but the lack of formal acceptance suggests procedural gaps contributed to vulnerability.
edges.evidenceGap: Evidence does not confirm whether Utilities or RHOB operations verified valve positions independently before relying on the pending release state.

tasks.target: What specific configuration drawing or change briefing did U-A and U-B review prior to the event window, and how was this information communicated?
tasks.decision: The proposed question seeks specific information about the configuration drawing or change briefing that U-A and U-B reviewed before the event window, focusing on what documentation they had access to during their preparation phase. Q5 most closely matches this intent by asking which configuration drawing revision was seen at work preparation time and whether it includes valves V-201/V-202; both questions target verification of actual equipment index referenced versus installed hardware status through examination of specific drawings available to the crew.

tasks.target: What was the exact sequence of events leading to the air-loss event, and who observed or recorded each step?
tasks.decision: The proposed question addresses a distinct investigative need—establishing a verified timeline of operator actions and observation recording completeness during the incident window—that cannot be satisfied by any single existing duplicate. Q1 covers pre-alarm preparation steps (09:48–10:00), while other duplicates focus on technical ambiguities, procedural compliance, or fault location determination rather than the specific evidence need for a complete action/observation timeline.

tasks.target: Was the recorder at C-11 present during the event, and if not, what alternative means were used to verify compressor state?
tasks.decision: The proposed question is equivalent to Q4 because both seek independent confirmation of recorder location during the event. S1 provides direct testimony that the recorder was not present and relied on screen labels/radio calls, satisfying the need established by either question.

tasks.target: Does the point register or any other record map AL-44 to a specific valve, line segment, or control logic that would explain why pressure at P-R dropped while C-11 remained running?
tasks.decision: The proposed question is not equivalent to any existing duplicate because it specifically asks for identification of a specific valve, line segment, or control logic that explains the pressure drop while C-11 remained running. Q6 focuses on whether AL-44 mapping excludes other inputs and clarifies alarm input sources but does not explicitly seek which physical component (valve/line) caused the event; it seeks to clarify if legacy display text or alternative inputs triggered false positives rather than identifying a specific valve failure in the distribution path. Q2 addresses ruling out alternatives like leaks vs valve failures using available data, focusing on whether source-side trip vs downstream loss is supported by evidence but does not explicitly seek identification of which component failed; it focuses more on determining if leak remains plausible or closed upstream valves support other hypotheses rather than identifying a specific valve/line/control logic. The proposed question's intent to identify the physical cause (valve, line segment, control logic) differs from Q2's focus on ruling out alternatives and Q6's focus on alarm input mapping exclusions.

tasks.target: Were valves V-201 or V-202 installed on the 1SC service route after ECP-1SC-04 revision 3 was issued, and if so, were they included in any temporary instruction attached to WO-527?
tasks.decision: No equivalent found among Q1–Q6 because none simultaneously address (a) whether V-201/V-202 were installed after revision 3, and (b) their inclusion in a temporary instruction for WO-527. Each duplicate focuses on either physical presence, documentation completeness alone, or issuance status without the combined procedural gap focus.

tasks.target: What is the exact service association of C-11 RUN (e.g., does it indicate only motor rotation, or also verify that all downstream isolation valves are open)?
tasks.decision: The question seeks specific technical definition of C-11 RUN's signal mapping and functional coverage. Existing duplicates address procedural documentation gaps or physical verification actions, not the point-register-defined scope of a running-status bit.

tasks.target: Does the absence of V-201 or V-202 in ECP-1SC-04 revision 3 equipment index indicate these valves are not part of the normal service route, or that a change disposition was never issued for their inclusion?
tasks.decision: Merge with Q6 because it provides clearer operational framing: it anchors the omission in S1, connects to incident location/time (RHOB receiving station), and directs analysis toward determining if V-201/V-202 are on normal service route or auxiliary lines that could affect P-R pressure. This satisfies both entity scope and decision need better than other duplicates.

tasks.target: What physical evidence exists to confirm whether the pressure drop at P-R was caused by a valve closure, line rupture, or upstream supply interruption?
tasks.decision: No duplicate question satisfies the proposed question's need for physical evidence distinguishing valve closure from line rupture versus upstream interruption while maintaining local reference integrity; each candidate either omits a cause category, lacks maintenance boundary context, cites external finding IDs not in S set, or frames as sufficiency rather than causal discrimination.

tasks.target: Was the work boundary for WO-527 physically isolated before the pressure loss, or was it only administratively prepared?
tasks.decision: No equivalent duplicate found; question remains open for investigation.

tasks.target: What evidence establishes whether V-201 or V-202 were installed in the distribution path to RHOB, and if so, what configuration drawing revision was issued for them?
tasks.decision: Merge the proposed question into Q5 because both seek evidence on whether V-201/V-202 were installed post-revision and if they are documented in change records or temporary instructions. Answering Q5 satisfies the intent of the proposed question.

tasks.target: What evidence establishes whether the pressure drop at P-R was caused by a valve closure, a leak, or a control signal failure?
tasks.decision: The proposed question is unique because it specifically enumerates 'valve closure', 'leak', or 'control signal failure' as the three potential mechanisms to distinguish, with an intent to differentiate between mechanical blockage/release and electrical/control-induced isolation. None of Q1-Q6 fully replicate this exact tripartite distinction while maintaining identical scope regarding maintenance boundary preparation context (S3/S5) and control-signal mapping issues (C-11 RUN bit vs actual trip). Each duplicate question omits at least one element: either the specific 'control signal failure' mechanism, or explicit inclusion of all three causes in a single discrimination task.

tasks.target: What evidence establishes whether the compressor C-11 was tripped or remained running during the pressure drop at P-R?
tasks.decision: The proposed question is distinct from all possible duplicates because it focuses solely on verifying whether C-11 was tripped or running, without addressing the specific sub-question in Q1 regarding 'COMP FAULT' label interpretation. It does not match the broader cause-discrimination intent of Q2-Q6 nor the alternative-failure-mode focus of Q4.

tasks.target: Does the absence of V-201/V-202 in ECP-1SC-04 revision 3's equipment index indicate those valves were not part of this maintenance boundary, or does it require a change record to confirm whether they should have been included?
tasks.decision: The proposed question should remain distinct because it specifically addresses whether missing valve entries necessitate a change record to confirm inclusion—a nuance not explicitly covered in Q2 (boundary acceptance) or Q6 (isolation procedure validity). The evidence packet does not provide sufficient information to merge this question with existing duplicates without losing its unique investigative focus.

tasks.target: Was the compressor C-11 tripped or did it continue running while supply pressure dropped below 4.5 bar, and if so, what upstream condition (e.g., header loss P-U) caused the drop?
tasks.decision: No equivalent duplicate found. The proposed question requires evidence of both compressor trip status and upstream supply path integrity (e.g., P-U stability vs. header loss), which is not fully satisfied by any single existing Q; S6 supports the pressure drop observation but does not independently establish an upstream cause without valve-state or flow-path data.

tasks.target: What is the current status of any temporary instruction attached to WO-527, and does it specify which valves were isolated or left open during maintenance preparation?
tasks.decision: No existing duplicate matches both parts (temporary instruction attachment status AND specified valve states) required by the proposed question; a distinct answer is needed.

tasks.target: Local indication returned to normal band.
tasks.decision: The condition represents a localized supply interruption that warrants further investigation into equipment state and work-boundary procedures. No definitive cause is established in this packet.

tasks.target: Local indication returned to normal band.
tasks.decision: The node is supported by S1, which documents the return of local indication to normal band at approximately 10:07.

tasks.target: Was compressor C-11 running at the time of pressure loss, and if so, was it supplying air to P-R or had its output been isolated?
tasks.decision: C-11 was running but its contribution to P-R pressure cannot be confirmed; a localized supply interruption downstream of P-U is supported by stable upstream readings and dropped downstream readings.

tasks.target: Did the pressure drop originate at P-U (site header) or between P-U and P-R?
tasks.decision: The pressure drop originated in the distribution path between upstream header P-U (site header H-U) and downstream receiving station P-R, as evidenced by stable P-U readings (~6.9 bar) concurrent with significant P-R drops (<3.5 bar). This rules out an interruption at P-U itself.

tasks.target: Were any valves in the 1SC distribution route (e.g., M-101, M-102) open or closed during maintenance preparation?
tasks.decision: The investigation question asks for valve positions in the distribution route. The evidence packet contains no record of field observations or measurements that would establish whether M-101/M-102 were open or closed at the time of maintenance preparation. Existing documents (ECP index, work package cover) list equipment but do not capture real-time states.

tasks.target: Was an approved temporary instruction attached to WO-527 at the time of initial notification?
tasks.decision: The work package cover (WO-527) shows the temporary instruction attachment field is blank at issue time and no approved temporary instruction was attached. This satisfies the question's premise that an approved TI was not present.

tasks.target: Did the pressure drop originate at the source, distribution system, or receiving equipment?
tasks.decision: The origin point remains undetermined because available evidence only confirms a localized pressure loss between stable upstream supply and low receiving station, without identifying the specific component or location where interruption began. The initial notification explicitly lacks this detail.

tasks.target: Was the work boundary formally released before the pressure loss occurred?
tasks.decision: Evidence S1 and S3 establish that the work boundary was not formally released before the pressure loss occurred; it remained in a 'preparation only' state with maintenance acceptance pending. The decision is supported by direct desk entries recording release as pending at approximately 09:48, prior to the incident window.

tasks.target: Did the pressure loss originate at the air source, within the distribution system (e.g., a valve closure or leak), or at the receiving equipment?
tasks.decision: The upstream stability (S10) rules out source failure. The drop magnitude and timing suggest a localized event in the distribution path, but without valve state or flow data, exact origin remains unknown.

tasks.target: Was the maintenance boundary for WO-527 formally released before the pressure loss occurred?
tasks.decision: Evidence S1 and S3 establish that the boundary was in 'preparation only' state with no acceptance signature at notification time (09:48–10:02). The absence of a signed ECP-1SC-04 or other release record means formal release had not occurred before pressure loss.

tasks.target: Was there any evidence suggesting that the air supply interruption began at the receiving equipment rather than upstream?
tasks.decision: Evidence indicates a localized pressure loss but does not confirm whether it began upstream in the distribution path or downstream near RHOB; no evidence supports receiving-equipment origin.

tasks.target: Did the pressure values recorded in ⟦evidence:span:1ccc6519-6aaf-4b86-a53d-d6d1d3abb7c7:39fc6db3a8d03c1f:0-1054⟧ confirm a significant drop at P-R around 10:00 AM?
tasks.decision: The pressure data in S1 directly supports the premise of a significant drop at P-R around 10:00 AM, with upstream stability indicating a localized issue rather than total system failure.

tasks.target: Was there any documented change in valve positions, isolation status, or equipment configuration during the maintenance preparation that could have contributed to the instrument-air pressure drop?
tasks.decision: The investigation question regarding a documented change in valve positions cannot be answered affirmatively with current evidence. The available records confirm that no formal release was granted, but they do not contain field execution logs showing specific actions taken by U-A or U-B on valves V-201/V-202/M-101/D-101 during the preparation phase.

tasks.target: What specific mechanism caused the pressure drop at P-R (e.g., compressor trip, valve closure, distribution leak)?
